activity.notes: Caratacus was not securely a hereditary king of the Silures. After the Roman invasion of AD 43 he escaped west and renewed resistance among the Silures; under governor Ostorius Scapula (from 47) he became the leading anti-Roman commander, before defeat and capture in AD 51. ATLAS therefore records active_in with a resistance-leader role rather than 'King of the Silures'.

sources.title: Caratacus — Oxford Classical Dictionary
sources.citation_text: The Oxford Classical Dictionary states that Caratacus escaped west to the Silures, renewed hostilities against Ostorius Scapula, and was defeated and surrendered to Rome in 51.

sources.title: Caratacus — British Museum
sources.citation_text: The British Museum identifies Caratacus as an Iron Age ruler and resistance leader who was finally defeated about AD 51.
